dsh-subagents-model

See which model a DeepSeek Harness session is really running on. A chip in the
header names the mode

l and reasoning effort of whichever conversation is open —
including a subagent's — a chip in the co

mposer dock below the composer shows
which models a whole run delegated to, and sidebar hover cards

say what each
conversation actually did. It only ever ADDS controls: the harness's own
subagent drop
down is left exactly as shipped.
## If nothing appears

Every failure mode this plugin has had was silent — no error, no log, just an
absent chip — so here
is the order to check:

1. **Restart the profile.** The bundle is composed at boot, not on save.
2. **Confirm it is enabled*

* in Settings → Plugins.
[该节后续省略]
## What it shows
| seat | what it shows | where |
| **header chip** | `model: <id> (effort)` for the **active** Session | beside the subagent pill in

the conversation header |
| **bottom-bar chip** | how many subagents this run delegated to, and whic

h models they ran on | `conversation.composer.dock`, below the composer beside the ContextMeter |
|
**hover-card rows** | model, effort, work done, active time, tokens, cache, context window, task, ki
nd | inside every Session's hover card in the sidebar |

The chip's tooltip also names the reasoning efforts a model offers and which one
is its default, rea

d from the live model catalog. A model the catalog does not
list adds nothing: the catalog is adviso

ry and routing accepts ids it does not
advertise, so its absence is never treated as a fault.

The effort appears only when one is set — it is optional on the same route record
the model comes fr
om, and a session with none configured stays compact.

Presentation only. The model, its tools, and its session log are untouched: no
tool is registered, n

o service is published, and nothing the model can observe
changes.
## Three seats, and why none of them replaces anything

Every seat ADDS a cell with its own `id`, so no shipped occupant is displaced
and the harness's own

subagent dropdown is left exactly as shipped. That is not
an aesthetic choice: an earlier version of

this plugin claimed the
`subagent-catalog` header cell at `priority: -9998` in order to put a model

marker beside each subagent row, because the shipped `CatalogRows` renders no
per-row slot (`dsh-cl

ient-ui-subagent/lib/client.js:164-338`). Replacing that
cell means reimplementing its entire naviga

tion contract — `openChild`,
`openChildAside`, `refreshProjection`, the tree walk, the focus model —

and every
mistake in that reimplementation removes the **stock subagent list** from the
header. It
did; the list stopped appearing.

The per-subagent model breakdown now lives in the bottom-bar chip instead, which
needs none of that

machinery. `scripts/check-plugin.mjs` asserts that nothing
claims or shadows a shipped cell, so the
takeover cannot quietly return.

| `conversation.session.header.actions` | `dsh-client-ui-conversation/lib/index.js:18268-18271` | `i

d 'subagent-model'` (chip) |
| `conversation.composer.dock` | `dsh-client-ui-conversation/lib/index.

js:18329-18332` | `id 'subagent-model-dock'` at `order 40` (bottom bar) |
| `sidebar.session.row.hov
er` | `dsh-client-ui-workspace/lib/index.js:4322-4325` | `id 'subagent-model'` |
## What each seat tells you

**The chip** names the effective route of whichever conversation is open, root or
subagent, and mark

s it `(switching)` while a queued selection has not been
consumed, `(inherited)` when it came from a

parent. Its tooltip adds the model
breakdown across descendants — `3× deepseek-chat, 2× deepseek-re

asoner` — and,
when a generation actually splits that breakdown, the same breakdown cut by
generatio

n. That is the integration with the sibling `dsh-subagent-tree`: both
facts come from one walk over
`subagentCatalog`, so they read in one place.

**The bottom-bar chip** answers the same question for the whole run rather than
for the conversation

that happens to be open: how many subagents this session
delegated to, and which models they ran on

. It lives in
`conversation.composer.dock`, the row below the composer beside the built-in
ContextMe

ter — the same slot and the same control shape the sibling
`dsh-opencode-router` uses for its proxy

chip. It renders nothing at all for a
run that never delegated, so an ordinary conversation grows no

nothing at all for a
run that never delegated, so an ordinary conversation grows no extra furniture.

**The hover card** answers "what was this conversation". Each row is read from a
projection the clie

nt already holds and appears only when its value is present,
so a zero never reads as "did nothing":

model and effort, turns and steps, active
time, generated tokens, the delegating agent's own task l

abel, and the mode that
decides whether the session can be continued.
### Why the pure logic lives in a second chunk

A classic script cannot `import`, but it does not have to: the `require` the
factory is handed carri

es an `async` method that fetches a package-local chunk
(`dsh-client-modules/lib/client.js:707-713`)

, and `CLIENT_CHUNK =
/^client\.[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*\.js$/` (`:169`, served at `:915-932`) is

the
pattern that file has to match. Three shipped packages already ship a second
chunk this way — `d

sh-client-ui-sidebar-terminal` and
`dsh-client-ui-sidebar-documentpreview` — so this is a supported

shape, not a
workaround.

`src/model.js` is a plain ESM module, which no browser script can reach, so
`src/client.model.js` ho

lds the same functions as a self-registering chunk and
`src/client.js` loads it once. The duplicatio

n was previously the whole cost of
shipping both; it is now confined to one chunk whose exports are

checked against
`src/model.js`.

Every seat renders nothing until that chunk resolves, which is what keeps a
failed fetch from taking

the conversation header down. The trade is that the chip
appears a tick later than a sync import wo

uld allow; nothing else on the page
waits on it.
